newsitem.title: FRANCE: Publicis settles dispute with True North.
newsitem.headline: Publicis settles dispute with True North.

text.p: French advertising agency Publicis said on Thursday it had settled a year-long dispute with its former U.S. ally True North, parent of Foote, Cone & Belding (FCB), the largest U.S. advertising agency.
Both companies will withdraw their respective legal claims against each other, it said.

Publicis will now develop a global network of agencies under its own name. It will transfer to True North the FCB agencies in Paris, London, Lisbon and Athens where Publicis already has a strong presence.

True North said that it will now form a new European network by uniting the four FCB offices it and Publicis formerly ran with Wilkens International, a 19-country pan-European advertising network bought in January.

"We have got our own 100 percent-managed network in Europe which we haven't had for the last 10 years," Harry Reid, president of True North Communications International, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The accord gives Publicis ownership of the rest of the FCB European venture not transferred to True North. True North will transfer to Publicis "a portion" of its 49 percent stake in Publicis FCB.
The rest of the stake will be converted to give True North 26.5 percent of Publicis Communication, Publicis SA's advertising operating unit, up from 20.8 percent previously.
Publicis will maintain its 20 percent stake in True North and will be its largest shareholder. Both companies will have a seat on each other's board of directors.
"It's a very agreeable restatement of our working partnership with Publicis," Reid said.
The row between the two firms broke out publicly a year ago. But Reid said reports of infighting had been overdone.
"Some of the acrimony has been very inaccurate. The partnership in terms of client service has been fantastic... it hasn't been World War Three for sure," he said.

The disagreement dates back over a year, prompted by a feeling on both sides that certain aspects of the agreement had been broken and "something had happened to the spirit of partnership", Reid said.
Both companies were now free to forge whatever alliances they wished to, he added. The continuing link between True North and Publicis would still serve both groups.
True North would have revenue from its Publicis stake, and the alliance would help it particularly in markets like media buying, where size was becoming important, he said.
Publicis, which is just starting up its international network, will still be able to call on True North for servicing in places where it has not yet set up its own agency.
Under the accord, Publicis's European network will take the name of Publicis Europe and will be wholly-owned by Publicis Communication.

True North will also sell to Publicis its interest in the South African agency, The Partnership, and a majority interest in agencies either existing or to be spun-off from existing agencies in Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, India and Thailand.
